name: Can rotted logs be repaired during the refinishing process?

mainEntity.name: Can rotted logs be repaired during the refinishing process?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor surface softness can often be treated, stabilized with wood hardeners, and sealed, but deep structural rot requires cutting out compromised log sections and splicing in fresh timber. During refinishing, an experienced carpenter inspects logs for hollow spots or insect channels. HH Remodeling brings general contracting and custom framing capabilities to the project, meaning structural carpentry repairs can be completed directly alongside surface restoration rather than requiring separate contractors to stabilize the building before staining can resume.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Minor rot can be stabilized, while severe rot requires cutting out damaged wood and splicing in new timber, which can be done as part of the overall refinishing project.
